title: Heuristic-driven stage latency equalizer for multi-GPU token waves
creator: Asha Gupta
description: Problem: On heterogeneous multi-GPU nodes we observe bursty tail latency during prefill->decode transitions when stages fall out of alignment. Small differences in per-stage kernel choice and queue servicing lead to token-wave drift, reducing achievable NCCL overlap and increasing per-token cost. Existing schedulers rely on static heuristics (fixed micro-wait, simple round-robin) which either waste GPU cycles or force serialization.
goal: Introduce a lightweight heuristic controller (Stage Latency Equalizer, SLE) that measures per-stage effective latency distribution and dynamically injects micro-pacing and kernel-probing decisions to re-align token waves across tensor/pipeline parallel stages, maximizing NCCL overlap while preserving decode latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 95th percentile end-to-end prefill+decode latency reduced by >= 12% on heterogeneous 4-GPU A100/RTX mixes under synthetic token-wave load
2) NCCL send/recv overlapping window utilization improved by >= 18% vs baseline measured with trace sampler
3) No more than 2% regression in median latency for low-concurrency steady-state workloads
4) Controlled fallback to conservative scheduling when SLE confidence is low (safety gate), with logs and metrics surfaced in Console
5) Unit/integration tests cover kernel-probing and pacing backoff logic and pass in CI across GPU topology matrix
implementation_notes: SLE has three cooperating mechanisms: (A) per-stage lightweight latency profiler (sampling every N requests) that reports effective kernel+queue time; (B) a kernel-probing policy that opportunistically runs alternative kernel variants on a small shadow batch to estimate delta cost/latency; (C) a pacing controller that injects computed micro-waits on faster stages (or nudges slower stages via micro-batching) to equalize stage service time. Controller state is per-node and per-model-version; control loop runs at 100-300ms cadence. Key touchpoints: scheduler (steering), runtime kernel registry, NCCL overlap estimator, and Console metrics pipeline. Safety: confidence scoring and exponential backoff when variance grows. Fallback: revert to topology-aware token sharding when SLE disabled.
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed — micro-benchmark harness for heterogeneous 4-GPU mix implemented. Observed 20-40ms per-stage skew under synthetic 1k token prefills.

2026-02-25: Prototype pacing controller added to local branch. Early tests show 10% improvement in NCCL overlap but occasional throughput regressions at high concurrency. Investigating probing frequency.
2026-03-01: Kernel-probing module merged to feature branch; introduced shadow batch probing to avoid perturbing live requests. Added confidence scoring based on probe variance.

2026-03-04: Canary run on gpu-pool-staging with mixed A100+V100 nodes. 95th P latency median improved 13% across 40-minute job; two regressions tied to noisy host processes — added host noise detector and adaptive threshold.
2026-03-05: Preparing PR for runtime-1.22; writing integration tests for topology matrices and adding Console dashboards for overlap/utilization metrics. Planning rollback criteria for canary.

qa_plan: Create deterministic replay harness that can inject per-stage perturbations and validate SLE decisions. Run across topology matrix (4x A100, 2xA100+2xV100, 8xRTX) with token lengths [64,512,2048] and concurrency points [1,8,32]. Smoke tests for fallback behavior and CI gating for kernel-probing experiments.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag default off. 2) Internal canaries on staging node pools. 3) Gradual ramp to low-traffic production pools with health checks (latency SLO, NCCL overlap, CPU host noise). 4) Metrics-driven ramp including automatic disable if overlap decreases for 10 consecutive minutes.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Probing could perturb latency if misconfigured — mitigate by shadow probing and conservative probe rate. Risk: Host-level noise may mislead controller — add host noise detector and require multi-sample consensus. Risk: Interaction with existing batchers — integrate with batching coordinator and add opt-out tag for routes requiring deterministic latency.
next_steps: Finish integration tests, land PR for runtime-1.22 branch, add Console panels and alerts, schedule canary for 2026-03-10, coordinate with infra for trace sampler rollout.
notes: This ticket takes a different approach from prior work (staggered rendezvous and comm-slicing) by focusing on small, closed-loop pacing decisions driven by measured kernel performance and probe signals rather than coarse global scheduling changes. The controller is intentionally lightweight to be safe for Private deployments where operator control matters.
